name: Quinine skin lightener

lead: Quinine is mentioned as an ingredient found in some illegal skin-lightening products, alongside steroids and mercury compounds.
No studies of it as a skin lightener were found.

paras: No mechanism for skin lightening is described in the sources reviewed.

Products in the illicit market are reported to contain hazardous ingredients such as mercury and potent steroids, and regulators in several countries have acted against them. Quinine-specific harms in this use were not documented in the sources reviewed.

lead: Quinine has been reported as an ingredient in some skin-lightening products sold illegally, alongside corticosteroids, mercury compounds and bleach-based preparations [1]. Wikipedia's skin whitening article mentions it in the context of a 1997 Paris police crackdown on illegal trafficking of such products [1].
The sources reviewed give no information on how quinine would lighten skin, on any trials, or on its specific harms in this use.
infobox: Ingredient reported in illicit lightening products
Products containing it were targeted in illegal-trade enforcement [1]

paras: Skin lightening products have drawn regulatory attention for ingredients including mercury, hydroquinone and potent corticosteroids. The EU banned hydroquinone in cosmetics in 2000, and several countries restrict mercury-containing products, though enforcement varies and such products remain sold online [1]. Quinine appears in the article only as one of the substances found in the illegal market [1].

timeline.event: Paris police crackdown on illegal trafficking of lightening products, some containing quinine, corticosteroids or mercury [1].
